title: Picard groups of products with an affine-cell proper variety
statement:
Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field], [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $X$ be a smooth proper geometrically integral $F$-scheme [def-pc-scheme], [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], [def-weil-proper-morphism], [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. Suppose that $X$ contains a dense open subscheme $U\cong\mathbf A^d_F$ for some $d\geq0$ [def-weil-open-immersion], [def-sbc-affine-space]; dense means its closure is all of $X$. Let $T$ be a smooth geometrically integral separated finite-type $F$-scheme [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Geometrically integral means nonempty and integral after every field extension. For any scheme $Y$, write $\operatorname{Pic}(Y)$ for the abelian group of isomorphism classes of invertible $\mathcal O_Y$-modules, with addition induced by tensor product; invertible means Zariski locally free of rank one [def-sc-invertible-module]. For the projections $p_X:X\times_F T\to X$ and $p_T:X\times_F T\to T$ [def-pc-fibre-product], tensor pullback [def-pc-module-pullback] induces an isomorphism of abelian groups
$$\operatorname{Pic}(X)\oplus\operatorname{Pic}(T)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Pic}(X\times_F T),\qquad ([M],[N])\longmapsto[p_X^*M\otimes p_T^*N].$$
In particular, if $t_0\in T(F)$ and an invertible sheaf $H$ on $X\times_F T$ has $H|_{X\times\{t_0\}}\cong L$ for an invertible sheaf $L$ on $X$, then $H\cong p_X^*L\otimes p_T^*N$ for some invertible sheaf $N$ on $T$.

source.place: Agent-formulated product consequence of Tag 02TT (lemma-pullback-affine-fibres-surjective), Tag 02RX (lemma-restrict-to-open), and the identification Cl=CH in section-divisor-invertible-sheaf; divisors.tex Tag 0BE9 (lemma-local-rings-UFD-c1-bijective). Smoothness gives regular local factorial rings. The boundary argument extends Milne Lemma 18.21, printed p.392, to products; its full argument is retained in report.md.

proof.text: Both $X$ and $T$ are regular and locally Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-scheme-over-field-regular]. They are separated and of finite type over $F$ (for $X$ these follow from properness). By [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-over-affine] they are quasi-compact and quasi-separated, hence Noetherian. By [lem-sc-separated-over-affine-scheme-separated] they are also separated over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$. Their structure morphisms are locally of finite presentation by [lem-pc-smooth-flat], and therefore of finite presentation. Choose $x_0\in U(F)$ as the origin of the specified affine cell and choose $t_*\in T(F)$ by [lem-pc-rational-points-dense], since $T$ is nonempty and $F$ is algebraically closed.

source.place: Tag 056S, lemma-smooth-regular; finite type and separated conventions; rational points as in the cited density lemma.

proof.text: Put $W=X\times_FT$. Both projections are smooth by [lem-pc-proper-base-change], flat and locally of finite presentation by [lem-pc-smooth-flat], and universally open by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-lfp-open]. They are of finite presentation by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence], applied to the finite-presentation structure maps of step 1. The projection $p_X$ is separated and of finite type by [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change]; composition with $X\to\operatorname{Spec}F$ is of finite type by [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change]. Its geometric fibres are the base changes of $T$, hence nonempty and integral. Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-integral-fibre-vertical-divisors] with base $X$ and dense open $U$: $W$ is regular and locally Noetherian, and $W_U=U\times_FT$ is dense. Moreover $W$ is integral by [lem-sfb-integral-pullback-geometric-flat-open], with $X\to\operatorname{Spec}F$ the geometrically integral flat universally open morphism and $T$ the integral locally Noetherian base.

source.place: Tag 00ON, lemma-dimension-base-fibre-equals-total, as packaged by the cited vertical-divisor lemma; smooth and finite-presentation base change.

proof.text: Identify $A=W_U=\mathbf A^d_T$ and let $q:A\to T$ be projection. It is smooth by [sbc-lem-affine-space-smooth]. It is separated and of finite presentation: over each affine $\operatorname{Spec}R\subset T$ it is $\operatorname{Spec}R[z_1,\ldots,z_d]\to\operatorname{Spec}R$, with the displayed finite polynomial presentation; its diagonal is cut out by $z_i-z_i'$. Every fibre after any field extension is affine space over a field, and is nonempty and integral because a polynomial ring over a field is a domain. Applying [lem-sfb-smooth-integral-fibre-vertical-divisors] with base $T$ and dense open $T$ gives regularity and local Noetherianity of $A$. It is quasi-compact since it has the finite affine cover obtained from a finite affine cover of $T$. For integrality apply [lem-sfb-integral-pullback-geometric-flat-open] to $\mathbf A^d_F\to\operatorname{Spec}F$ and $T$, using [lem-pc-smooth-flat] and [lem-weil-pbc-flat-lfp-open].

source.place: Tag 0BDA, lemma-open-subscheme-UFD, for affine-space fibres; polynomial presentation and the cited smooth/regular geometric inputs.

proof.text: The schemes $W$ and $A$ are separated over $F$: under the product identifications, the diagonal of $W$ is defined by imposing the two closed diagonal conditions for $X$ and $T$, and the diagonal of $A\to T$ is the polynomial diagonal of step 3. These conditions are closed immersions on affine charts (the corresponding ring maps are the evident quotient maps). Composing the two diagonal conditions proves separatedness of the structure maps to $F$. Thus [lem-sc-separated-over-affine-scheme-separated] makes them separated over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$. Since $W$ is of finite type over $F$, it is quasi-compact, and with its established local Noetherianity it is Noetherian. Both $A$ and $W$ are therefore regular integral Noetherian separated schemes of finite type over $F$.

source.place: Tag 01KK, definition-separated: explicit product and composite diagonal calculation; Tag 01KU, lemma-separated-permanence.

proof.text: Let $H$ be any invertible sheaf on $W$. For $K=F(T)$, the generic fibre of $q$ is $\mathbf A^d_K$, so [lem-sfb-affine-space-invertible-trivial], applied over the field $K$, trivializes $H|_{\mathbf A^d_K}$. Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-generic-trivial-line-descent] to $q:A\to T$ and $H|_A$. Its hypotheses were verified in steps 1, 3 and 4; surjectivity follows also from the zero section. It gives an invertible sheaf $N$ on $T$ and $H|_A\cong q^*N$. Put $H'=H\otimes(p_T^*N)^{-1}$, which is trivial on $A$. Tensor products, duals and pullbacks of these locally rank-one modules are again locally rank one: in a local basis their modules are the coefficient ring, and evaluation sends the basis and its dual to $1$.

source.place: Tag 0BDA, lemma-open-subscheme-UFD; generic-fibre descent as in the cited 00ON/0AGA vertical-divisor consequence.

proof.text: Choose a trivialization $s$ of $H'$ over the dense open $A$. It is a nonzero rational section on the integral $W$. By [lem-sfb-regular-space-divisor-line-dictionary], its Weil divisor $D_W=\operatorname{div}(s)$ is a finite integral sum of prime divisors, has support outside $A$ (the section is everywhere a generator on $A$), and $H'\cong\mathcal O_W(D_W)$. Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-integral-fibre-vertical-divisors] to $p_X:W\to X$ and $U\subset X$. All its hypotheses were checked in steps 1 and 2. Its supported-divisor isomorphism gives a divisor $D_X$ on $X$ supported outside $U$ with $D_W=p_X^*D_X$. The dictionary gives the invertible $M=\mathcal O_X(D_X)$, and its flat-pullback compatibility gives $p_X^*M\cong\mathcal O_W(p_X^*D_X)\cong H'$. Hence $H\cong p_X^*M\otimes p_T^*N$.

source.place: Tag 0AGA, lemma-weil-divisor-is-cartier-UFD, and Tag 0BE9, lemma-local-rings-UFD-c1-bijective; the supported prime-divisor correspondence is the cited vertical-divisor lemma, based on algebra.tex Tag 00ON.

proof.text: The map in the statement is well-defined on isomorphism classes and is a group homomorphism. Indeed the pullback formula of [def-pc-module-pullback] commutes with tensor products: locally the identification is $(a\otimes m)\otimes(b\otimes n)\mapsto ab\otimes(m\otimes n)$, with inverse $c\otimes(m\otimes n)\mapsto(c\otimes m)\otimes(1\otimes n)$. The balanced relations verify the two inverse formulas, which agree on overlaps. Associativity and commutativity of tensor products of local rank-one modules then identify the image of a sum with the tensor product of the images. Step 6 proves surjectivity.

source.place: Tensor pullback formula and its elementary balanced-tensor identities.

proof.text: If $p_X^*M\otimes p_T^*N\cong\mathcal O_W$, pull back along $x\mapsto(x,t_*)$. By the composite-pullback identity of [def-pc-module-pullback] this gives $M\otimes\mathcal O_X\cong\mathcal O_X$, because the fibre $N_{t_*}$ is a one-dimensional $F$-vector space and a choice of a nonzero vector trivializes its constant pullback. Thus $M$ is trivial. Pulling back along $t\mapsto(x_0,t)$ similarly shows that $N$ is trivial. This proves injectivity, hence the homomorphism of step 7 is an isomorphism.

source.place: Composite pullback and pullback of a one-dimensional vector space; the two chosen rational-point sections.

proof.text: Finally suppose $t_0\in T(F)$ and $H|_{X\times\{t_0\}}\cong L$. By step 6 write $H\cong p_X^*M\otimes p_T^*N$. Pull back along $x\mapsto(x,t_0)$ and trivialize the one-dimensional vector space $N_{t_0}$ as in step 8. This gives $L\cong M$. Substituting this isomorphism gives $H\cong p_X^*L\otimes p_T^*N$, as required.

source.place: Elementary rational-fibre restriction of the external tensor product from step 6.
